headline: Pakistan to fly an astronaut on China's next space station mission
summary: Pakistan will send an astronaut on China's next space station mission, according to Al Jazeera on the seventh of November.
NASA has awarded Ka-band relay contracts to Viasat, SES and Astranis.
ArianeGroup has fired its Prometheus reusable engine on a German test bench.
Telesat has moved full Lightspeed service to mid-2028.
Europe's committee vote on the tenth of November is the next date on the road to Rome.
bottom_line: The Pakistani seat on a Chinese station mission is the one pathway that moved, and no crew name or launch date is on file. The next date that matters is the tenth of November, the European committee vote ahead of Rome on the fifteenth of December.
audio_script:
Good morning. It is Saturday, the seventh of November, and this is the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing. Pakistan will fly an astronaut on China's next space station mission. Europe's Prometheus reusable engine has passed a new hot-fire test. And NASA has awarded Ka-band relay contracts to three commercial firms.

A Pakistani astronaut will join China's next space station mission. Al Jazeera reported the announcement on the seventh of November. It gives no crew name and no launch date. It does not say how long the flight will last. This is a new pathway for South Asia in human spaceflight. The date to watch is the launch date for the mission, which has not been set out publicly.

In Europe, ArianeGroup fired its Prometheus reusable rocket engine on the fifth and sixth of November, on the P5 test bench run by the German space centre DLR. The company calls it a new development milestone. Prometheus is the engine behind Europe's reusable launcher work. On the European road to Rome, studies of a European-led orbital outpost were awarded on the third of November. The next step is the committee vote on the tenth of November, then the ministerial meeting in Rome on the fifteenth of December. Arianespace plans to launch thirty-six Amazon Leo satellites on the tenth Ariane 6 flight on the twenty-third of November at the earliest.

In Central and Eastern Europe, the question is satellite communications for Ukraine. Starshield has a stated hope of a contract in mid-2027. There has been no answer on what happened in October. No date has been set for a decision.

In the Nordics, Sweden's space agency has set its next Space Day for the eighteenth of February, 2027. The announcement was made on the second of November. Norway's space directorate has a new agreement with the Canadian Space Agency on Arctic cooperation, though its signing date is not on file.

In France, ArianeGroup reports a second successful launch of the SyLEx sounding rocket on the fourth of November. Spanish trade press links the launch to development of the M51.4 nuclear missile. No further SyLEx date is on file.

In Central Asia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan published no dated decisions this week. Turkish trade press says a joint satellite of Turkic states is due for launch in 2027. No launch month is given.

In Türkiye, a new Turkish microsatellite is due to launch in 2028. A separate report from the United States on Iran's space power was published on the fifth of November. Türkiye's proposed space and aviation budget for 2027 stands at 24.59 billion lira, with no split published.

In China, the CERES-2 rocket has been launched on its second attempt. Separately, China has sent up a new batch of internet satellites. Pakistan's seat on the next station flight is the larger development in the region.

In Paraguay, Paraguayan press says the second national satellite, GuaraniSat-2, has been launched. The first satellite, GuaraniSat-1, has completed its mission and re-entered. In Canada, Telesat has moved full Lightspeed service to mid-2028. In the United States, a return of Blue Origin's New Glenn in January 2027 is reported by the Financial Times and is unconfirmed by the company. The FAA comment deadline of the thirtieth of October has passed with no decision on file. For NASA, Artemis dates are unchanged, and commercial station proposals are due on the eighth of December.

What we are tracking this week: the European committee vote on the tenth of November, any launch date for the Pakistani astronaut, and any company confirmation of the New Glenn return. What we are tracking this month: the Amazon Leo launch on Ariane 6, no earlier than the twenty-third of November, and any FAA decision on Blue Origin. Heads-up dates: the eighth of December for NASA station proposals, the fifteenth of December for Rome, and the eighteenth of February for Sweden's Space Day. That is the briefing for Saturday, the seventh of November.

global.why: Launch availability is delaying a Canadian constellation. Sovereign demand is cited as continuing.
